key: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee, With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amrta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.
s: Once Agni is found in the loftiest station, the hymn turns to his secrets; Sāyaṇa, on 1.72.6, reads the ‘thrice-seven’ as twenty-one sacrifices, seven each of cooked food, of oblation and of Soma, placed in Agni alone because no rite can be done without fire.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.72.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 220672 (2019)

evidence.words: “त्रिः “सप्त एकविंशतिसंख्याकानि “गुह्यानि रहस्यानि वेदैकसमधिगम्यानि “यत् यानि “पदा पदानि । पद्यते गम्यते स्वर्गः एभिरिति व्युत्पत्त्या पदशब्देनात्र यज्ञा उच्यन्ते । ते चैकविंशतिसंख्याकाः। औपासनहोमवैश्वदेवादयः सप्त पाकयज्ञाः । अग्न्याधेयदर्शपूर्णमासादयः सप्त हविर्यज्ञाः । अग्निष्टोमात्यग्निष्टोमादयः सप्त सोमयज्ञाः । एवमेकविंशतिसंख्याकानि यज्ञलक्षणानि पदानि हे अग्न “त्वे “इत् त्वय्येव “निहिता स्थापितानि । तेषां सर्वेषां त्वत्प्रधानत्वात्। न ह्यग्निमन्तरेण यागा अनुष्ठातुं शक्यन्ते
evidence.gloss: Thrice seven: twenty-one in number; hidden: secret, to be learnt from the Veda alone; the padas: since heaven is reached (padyate) by them, pada here means sacrifices, and they are twenty-one: seven cooked-food sacrifices (pākayajña), aupāsana, homa, vaiśvadeva and the rest; seven oblation sacrifices (haviryajña), setting up the fires, the new- and full-moon rites and the rest; seven Soma sacrifices, agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest. These twenty-one steps that are sacrifices are placed, O Agni, in you alone, since you are chief in all of them; for without Agni no sacrifice can be performed.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.72.6, at [71,6]), the whole verse. The reading is Sāyaṇa’s at 1.72.6 word for word: tri sapta = twenty-one padas, which are sacrifices, seven pākayajñas, seven haviryajñas, seven somayajñas, placed in Agni alone (tvayy eva nihitāni) because without Agni no sacrifice can be performed; Wilson’s note c agrees. Changed only the context clause: the proposal’s ‘Once the gods have found the hidden Agni’ goes beyond the day’s text, where in Griffith 1.72.2 ‘The Gods ... found not him’ and it is ‘the mortal band’ that in 1.72.4 ‘found Agni standing in the loftiest station’, and ‘hidden’ is not in the passage. Now ‘Once Agni is found in the loftiest station’, in the passage’s own terms; 45 words; no four words of the key. Revision 220672 is dated 2019-12-30 by the Wikisource API, so the src year stands. Yāska: no verse of this hymn in Sarup’s list. Evidence re-found by machine in the packet. entry-check ok.
